newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dollar down, bonds firm on wage verdict.
newsitem.headline: Australian dollar down, bonds firm on wage verdict.

text.p: The Australian dollar eased and bonds firmed in initial response to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission's (AIRC) verdict to the "living wage" claim, which granted lower paid workers A$10 per week.
At 2.08 p.m. (0408 GMT) the dollar was US$0.7770/75 compared with US$0.7779/84 just before the AIRC announcement, while the June 10-year bond futures contract was 92.145 against a pre-verdict 92.125.
June bill futures also firmed, rising to 94.10 from 94.07, equating to a cash rate of 5.90 percent and compared with current 6.0 percent official interest rates.

Economists's expectations had centred on a A$12 per week outcome compared with the Federal government's A$8 per week proposal and the Australian Council of Trade Unions' proposed A$20 per week safety net increases over the next three years and 8.75 percent minimum rate adjustment.
